5.5: For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people who were born in the wilderness on the way as they came out of Mitsrayim had not been circumcised.
5.6: For the children of Yisra’ĕl walked forty years in the wilderness, till all the nation - the men of battle who came out of Mitsrayim - were consumed, because they did not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore not to show them the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had sworn to their fathers that He would give us, “a land flowing with milk and honey.”
5.7: And Yahoshua circumcised their sons whom He raised up in their place; for they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way.
5.8: And it came to be, when they had completed circumcising all the nation, that they stayed in their places in the camp till they were healed.
5.9: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Yahoshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Mitsrayim from you.” So the name of the place is called Gilgal to this day.
5.10: And the children of Yisra’ĕl camped in Gilgal, and performed the Pesaḥ on the fourteenth day of the month at evening on the desert plains of Yeriḥo.
5.11: And they ate of the stored grain of the land on the morrow after the Pesaḥ, unleavened bread and roasted grain on this same day.
5.12: And the manna ceased on the day after they had eaten the stored grain of the land. And the children of Yisra’ĕl no longer had manna, but they ate the food of the land of Kena’an that year.
5.13: And it came to be, when Yahoshua was by Yeriḥo, that he lifted his eyes and looked and saw a Man standing opposite him with His sword drawn in His hand. And Yahoshua went to Him and said to Him, “Are You for us or for our adversaries?”
5.14: And He said, “No, for I have now come as Captain of the host of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” And Yahoshua fell on his face to the earth and did obeisance, and said to Him, “What is Aḏoni saying to His servant?”
5.15: And the Captain of the host of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Yahoshua, “Take your sandal off your foot, for the place where you stand is qodesh.” And Yahoshua did so.

6.1: And Yeriḥo was shut up tight because of the presence of the sons of Yisra’ĕl - none going out, and none coming in.
6.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Yahoshua, “See! I have given Yeriḥo and its meleḵ, mighty brave men, into your hand.
6.3: “And you shall go around the city, all the men of battle going around the city once. Do this for six days.
6.4: “And let seven kohenim bear seven rams’ horns before the ark, and on the seventh day go around the city seven times while the kohenim blow the horns.
6.5: “And it shall be, when they make a long blast with the ram’s horn, and when you hear the sound of the horn, that all the people shout with a great shout. And the wall of the city shall fall down flat, and the people shall go up every man straight before him.”
6.6: And Yahoshua son of Nun called the kohenim and said to them, “Take up the ark of the Covenant, and let seven kohenim bear seven rams’ horns before the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
6.7: And he said to the people, “Pass over, and go around the city, and let him who is armed pass over before the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
6.8: And it came to be, when Yahoshua had spoken to the people, that the seven kohenim bearing the seven rams’ horns before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 passed over and blew the horns, and the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 went after them.
6.9: And the armed men went before the kohenim who blew the horns, and the rear guard came after the ark, going on and blowing the horns.
6.10: But Yahoshua had commanded the people, saying, “Do not shout or cause your voice to be heard, nor let any word come out of your mouth, until the day I say to you, ‘Shout!’ Then you shall shout.”
6.11: And the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 went around the city, going around once. And they came into the camp and stayed in the camp.
6.12: And Yahoshua rose early in the morning, and the kohenim took up the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.13: And seven kohenim bearing seven rams’ horns before the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 were walking, going on, and they blew the horns, and the armed men went before them. But the rear guard came after the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, going on, and blowing the horns.
6.14: And the second day they went around the city once and returned to the camp. Thus they did six days.
6.15: And it came to be on the seventh day that they rose early, about the dawning of the day, and went around the city seven times in this way. Only on that day they went around the city seven times.
6.16: And it came to be at the seventh time, when the kohenim blew the horns, that Yahoshua said to the people, “Shout, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given you the city!
6.17: “And the city shall be put under the ban, it and all that is in it belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Only Raḥaḇ the whore is to live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent.
6.18: “And you, by all means guard yourselves from that which is under the ban, lest you come under the ban when you take of that which is under the ban, and make the camp of Yisra’ĕl a curse, and shall trouble it.
6.19: “But all the silver and gold, and vessels of bronze and iron, are qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, they go into the treasury of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
6.20: And the people shouted when the ram’s horns were blown. And it came to be when the people heard the sound of the horn, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat. And the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they captured the city.
6.21: And they put under the ban all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.
6.22: And to the two men who had spied out the land Yahoshua said, “Go into the house of the woman, the whore, and from there bring out the woman and all that she has, as you swore to her.”
6.23: And the young men, the spies, went in and brought out Raḥaḇ, and her father, and her mother, and her brothers, and all that she had. So they brought out all her relatives and put them outside the camp of Yisra’ĕl.
6.24: And they burned the city and all that was in it with fire. Only the silver and gold, and the vessels of bronze and of iron, they put into the treasury of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.25: However, Yahoshua kept alive Raḥaḇ the whore, and her father’s household, and all that she had. And she dwelt in the midst of Yisra’ĕl to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Yahoshua sent to spy out Yeriḥo.
6.26: And Yahoshua warned them at that time, saying, “Cursed is the man before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who rises up and builds this city Yeriḥo - he lays its foundation with his first-born, and with his youngest he puts up its gates.”
6.27: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with Yahoshua, and a report about him was in all the land.

7.1: But the children of Yisra’ĕl committed a trespass regarding that which is under the ban, for Aḵan son of Karmi, son of Zaḇdi, son of Zeraḥ, of the tribe of Yahuḏah, took of that which is under the ban. And the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against the children of Yisra’ĕl.
7.2: Now Yahoshua sent men from Yeriḥo to Ai, which is beside Bĕyth Awen, on the east side of Bĕyth Ĕl, and spoke to them, saying, “Go up and spy out the land.” And the men went up and spied out Ai.
7.3: And they returned to Yahoshua and said to him, “Let not all the people go up, but let about two or three thousand men go up and smite Ai. Do not make all the people toil up there, for the people of Ai are few.”
7.4: And about three thousand men went up there from the people, but they fled before the men of Ai.
7.5: And the men of Ai smote about thirty-six men, for they pursued them from before the gate as far as Sheḇarim, and smote them on the descent. So the hearts of the people melted and became like water.
7.6: And Yahoshua tore his garments, and fell to the earth on his face before the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 until evening, both he and the elders of Yisra’ĕl, and they put dust on their heads.
7.7: And Yahoshua said, “Oh Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, why have You brought this people over the Yardĕn at all, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay beyond the Yardĕn!
7.8: “O Aḏonai, what do I say when Yisra’ĕl turns its back before its enemies,
7.9: and the Kena’anites and all the inhabitants of the land hear, and shall surround us, and cut off our name from the earth. What then do You do for Your great Name?”
7.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Yahoshua, “Rise up! Why are you lying on your face?
7.11: “Yisra’ĕl has sinned, and they have also transgressed My Covenant which I commanded them. And they have even taken some of that which is under the ban, and have both stolen and deceived, and also put it among their own goods.
7.12: “And the sons of Yisra’ĕl shall not be able to stand before their enemies. They are going to turn their backs before their enemies, for they have become accursed. I am not with you any more, unless you destroy that which is under the ban from your midst.
7.13: “Rise up, qadosh the people, and you shall say, ‘Qadosh yourselves for tomorrow, because thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “That which is under the ban is in your midst, O Yisra’ĕl. You are not able to stand before your enemies until you put away that which is under the ban out of your midst.”
7.14: ‘And you shall be brought near in the morning, according to your tribes. And it shall be, the tribe which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 takes comes according to clans. And the clan which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 takes comes by households. And the household which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 takes comes by men.
7.15: ‘And it shall be that he who is taken with that which is under the ban is burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and because he has committed wickedness in Yisra’ĕl.’ ”
7.16: So Yahoshua arose early in the morning and brought Yisra’ĕl by their tribes, and the tribe of Yahuḏah was taken, and he brought the clan of Yahuḏah, and he took the clan of the Zarḥites.
7.17: And he brought the clan of the Zarḥites by men, and Zaḇdi was taken.
7.18: And he brought his household by men, and Aḵan son of Karmi, son of Zaḇdi, son of Zeraḥ, of the tribe of Yahuḏah, was taken.
7.19: Then Yahoshua said to Aḵan, “My son, now give esteem to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, and make confession to Him. And please declare to me what you have done, do not hide it from me.”
7.20: So Aḵan answered Yahoshua and said, “Truly, I have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, and this is what I did:
7.21: “When I saw among the spoil a lovely garment from Shin’ar, and two hundred sheqels of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing fifty sheqels, I coveted them and took them. And see, they are hidden in the ground in the midst of my tent, with the silver under it.”
7.22: And Yahoshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. And see, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver under it.
7.23: And they took them from the midst of the tent, brought them to Yahoshua and to all the children of Yisra’ĕl, and laid them out before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.24: Then Yahoshua, and all Yisra’ĕl with him, took Aḵan son of Zeraḥ, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his donkeys, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had, and they brought them to the Valley of Aḵor.
7.25: And Yahoshua said, “Why have you troubled us? 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 troubles you today!” Then all Yisra’ĕl stoned him with stones. And they burned them with fire after they had stoned them with stones.
7.26: And they raised over him a great heap of stones, which remains to this day. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 turned from the fierceness of His displeasure. Therefore the name of that place has been called the Valley of Aḵor to this day.

8.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Yahoshua, “Do not be afraid, nor be discouraged. Take all the soldiers with you, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the meleḵ of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land.
8.2: “So you shall do to Ai and its meleḵ as you did to Yeriḥo and its meleḵ. Only its spoil and livestock you take as plunder for yourselves. Lay for yourselves ambush for the city, behind it.”
8.3: And Yahoshua and all the soldiers rose up, to go up to Ai. And Yahoshua chose thirty thousand mighty brave men and sent them away by night,
8.4: and commanded them, saying, “See, you are going to lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, but all of you shall be prepared,
8.5: while I and all the people who are with me approach the city. And it shall be, when they come out against us, as formerly, that we shall flee before them,
8.6: and they shall come out after us till we have drawn them from the city, as though saying, ‘They are fleeing before us as formerly.’ And we shall flee before them,
8.7: then you shall rise from the ambush and seize the city. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall give it into your hand.
8.8: “And it shall be, when you capture the city, that you burn the city with fire. Do according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. See, I have commanded you.”
8.9: And Yahoshua sent them out. And they went to lie in ambush, and stayed between Bĕyth Ĕl and Ai, on the west side of Ai. But Yahoshua stayed that night in the midst of the people.
8.10: And Yahoshua rose up early in the morning and inspected the people, and went up, he and the elders of Yisra’ĕl, before the people to Ai.
8.11: And all the soldiers who were with him went up and drew near, and came before the city and camped on the north side of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.
8.12: And he took about five thousand men and placed them in ambush between Bĕyth Ĕl and Ai, on the west side of the city.
8.13: So they stationed the people, all the army that was on the north of the city, and its rear guard on the west of the city, and Yahoshua went that night into the midst of the valley.
8.14: And it came to be, when the meleḵ of Ai saw it, that the men of the city hastened and rose up early and went out against Yisra’ĕl to battle, he and all his people, at an appointed place before the desert plain. But he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.
8.15: And Yahoshua and all Yisra’ĕl let themselves be beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness.
8.16: And all the people who were in Ai were called together to pursue them. And they pursued Yahoshua and were drawn away from the city.
8.17: So there was not a man left in Ai or Bĕyth Ĕl who did not go out after Yisra’ĕl, and they left the city open and pursued Yisra’ĕl.
8.18: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Yahoshua, “Stretch out the spear that is in your hand toward Ai, for I give it into your hand.” And Yahoshua stretched out the spear that he had in his hand toward the city,
8.19: and the ambush rose up quickly from their place, and they ran at the stretching out of his hand, and entered the city and took it, and hastened to burn the city with fire.
8.20: And the men of Ai looked behind them and saw the smoke of the city rising to the shamayim. And there was no power in them to flee this way or that way, for the people who had fled to the wilderness turned back on the pursuers.
8.21: For when Yahoshua and all Yisra’ĕl saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city went up, they turned back and smote the men of Ai.
8.22: The others also came out of the city against them, so they were in the midst of Yisra’ĕl, some on this side and some on that side. And they smote them until none were left, and none had escaped.
8.23: But the meleḵ of Ai they caught alive, and brought him to Yahoshua.
8.24: And it came to be, when Yisra’ĕl ended slaying all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they pursued them, and when they all had fallen by the edge of the sword until they were consumed, that all the Yisra’ĕlites returned to Ai and smote it with the edge of the sword.
8.25: And it came to be that all who fell that day, both men and women, were twelve thousand - all men of Ai.
8.26: And Yahoshua did not draw back his hand, with which he stretched out the spear, until he had put all the inhabitants of Ai under the ban.
8.27: Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Yisra’ĕl took as booty for themselves, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He had commanded Yahoshua.
8.28: And Yahoshua burned Ai and made it a heap forever, a ruin to this day.
8.29: And he hanged the meleḵ of Ai on a tree until evening. And at sunset Yahoshua commanded that they should take his corpse down from the tree, and throw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raise over it a great heap of stones, to this day.
8.30: And Yahoshua built an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl in Mount Ĕyḇal,
8.31: as Mosheh the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded the children of Yisra’ĕl, as it is written in the Book of the Torah of Mosheh, “an altar of unhewn stones over which no man has wielded iron.” And they offered on it burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and slaughtered peace offerings.
8.32: And there, in the presence of the children of Yisra’ĕl, he wrote on the stones a copy of the Torah of Mosheh, which he had written.
8.33: And all Yisra’ĕl - the sojourner as well as the native - with their elders and officers and judges, stood on either side of the ark before the kohenim, the Lĕwites, who bore the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Half of them were in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ĕyḇal, as Mosheh the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded before, that they should baraḵ the people of Yisra’ĕl.
8.34: And afterward he read all the Words of the Torah, the bireḵoth and the cursings, according to all that is written in the Book of the Torah.
8.35: There was not a word of all that Mosheh had commanded which Yahoshua did not read before all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl, with the women, and the little ones, and the sojourners who accompanied them.

9.1: And it came to be, when all the melaḵim who were beyond the Yardĕn, in the hills and in the low country and in all the coasts of the Great Sea toward Leḇanon - the Ḥittite and the Amorite, the Kena’anite and the Perizzite, the Ḥiwwite and the Yeḇusite - heard,
9.2: they gathered together to fight with Yahoshua and Yisra’ĕl with one accord.
9.3: And the inhabitants of Giḇ’on heard what Yahoshua had done to Yeriḥo and Ai,
9.4: and they acted slyly and went and pretended to be envoys. And they took old sacks on their donkeys, old wineskins torn and mended,
9.5: and old and patched sandals on their feet, and old garments on themselves. And all the bread of their provision was dry, it was crumbs.
9.6: And they went to Yahoshua, to the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to the men of Yisra’ĕl, “We have come from a far land, and now, make a covenant with us.”
9.7: But the men of Yisra’ĕl said to the Ḥiwwites, “It could be that you dwell in our midst, so how would we make a covenant with you?”
9.8: And they said to Yahoshua, “We are your servants.” And Yahoshua said to them, “Who are you, and where do you come from?”
9.9: So they said to him, “From a land very far off your servants have come, because of the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. For we have heard the report of Him, and all that He did in Mitsrayim,
9.10: and all that He had done to the two melaḵim of the Amorites who were beyond the Yardĕn, to Siḥon meleḵ of Ḥeshbon, and Oḡ meleḵ of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.
9.11: “So our elders and all the inhabitants of our land spoke to us, saying, ‘Take food with you for the journey, and go to meet them, and say to them, “We are your servants, and now, make a covenant with us.” ’
9.12: “This bread of ours we took hot for our provision from our houses on the day that we left to come to you. But now, see, it is dry and it is crumby.
9.13: “And these wineskins which we filled were new, and see, they are torn. And these our garments and our sandals have become old because of the very long journey.”
9.14: And the men of Yisra’ĕl took some of their food, but they did not ask the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.15: And Yahoshua made peace with them, and made a covenant with them to let them live, and the rulers of the congregation swore to them.
9.16: And it came to be at the end of three days, after they had made a covenant with them, that they heard that they were their neighbors who dwelt near them.
9.17: And the children of Yisra’ĕl departed and came to their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Giḇ’on, and Kephirah, and Be’ĕroth, and Qiryath Ye’arim.
9.18: But the children of Yisra’ĕl did not smite them, because the rulers of the congregation had sworn to them by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl. And all the congregation grumbled against the rulers.
9.19: But all the rulers said to all the congregation, “We have sworn to them by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, and we are unable to touch them now.
9.20: “Let us do this to them: We shall keep them alive, lest wrath be upon us because of the oath which we swore to them.”
9.21: And the rulers said to them, “Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and drawers of water for all the congregation, as the rulers had promised them.”
9.22: Then Yahoshua called for them, and he spoke to them, saying, “Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ yet you are dwelling in our midst?
9.23: “And now you are cursed, and you shall not cease from being slaves, and woodcutters and drawers of water for the House of my Elohim.”
9.24: And they answered Yahoshua and said, “Your servants were clearly told that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim commanded His servant Mosheh to give you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you. So we were very much afraid for our lives because of you, and have done this deed.
9.25: “And now, see, we are in your hands. Do with us as it seems good and right to do to us.”
9.26: And he did so to them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and they did not kill them.
9.27: And that day Yahoshua made them woodcutters and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, even to this day, at the place that He should choose.
